content: Saint Paul Hospital is a comprehensive medical facility located in the central area of Hanoi, the capital city of Vietnam. It was originally established during the period of French colonial rule in Indochina, which spanned the 19th and early 20th centuries. In 2001, the hospital received significant support from several United States-based non-governmental organizations, including Counterpart International, Project Hope, and World Medical Relief. These organizations provided medicines and medical equipment valued at USD 302,457 to enhance the hospital's emergency services. In January 2007, Norway, the United States, Japan, and the Netherlands collectively committed to donating 7 million US dollars to fund the creation of a state-of-the-art research center at the hospital. According to plans announced by the Hanoi Health Department, Saint Paul Hospital is set to undergo substantial upgrades. These include the construction of a six-story building with a capacity of 100 beds dedicated to the Therapeutics Ward, as well as a similar six-story building with 150 beds for the Pediatrics Ward. Additionally, the hospital's second branch is expected to accommodate 500 beds following its renovation.
